paragraphs.notes: This is the top table on the page. It carries no caption of its own, only the word "(fortgesetzt)" (continued). It is the continuation of Tabelle 3, whose caption is printed on page 4: "Tabelle 3: Bindungslängen [Å] und Bindungswinkel [°] der Kristallmodifikation I". Evidence: page 4 prints that caption and then the first part of the same four column block, ending mid list at "F(2)-C(10)-C(9) 114.6(2)"; this page opens with "(fortgesetzt)" and the same four column headers, and the sequence continues without a gap. Only the 28 rows printed on THIS page are recorded here; the rows on page 4 are not repeated. The block sits under a bare caption with no [00NN] marker of its own, so it is attached to the nearest preceding numbered paragraph, which is [0018] on page 3. Tabellen 1 to 6 all fall under [0018] for the same reason. COLUMN STRUCTURE, read off the page image and not off the text layer: four columns, printed as two side by side pairs, headed Bindung | Å(°) | Bindung | Å(°). The text layer flattens all four into one row major run, which destroys the pairing; the digits below were confirmed against the text layer but the association of label to value was read from the image. The right hand pair stops after 17 rows; rows 18 to 28 have the right hand pair blank on the page, and the empty cells recorded here are what is printed, not data that could not be read. UNITS: the shared heading "Å(°)" carries two units at once, and which one applies is determined by the LABEL, not by the column. A two atom label such as F(3)-C(10) is a bond LENGTH in Angstrom. A three atom label such as F(1)-C(10)-C(9) is an ANGLE in degrees. The unit switches partway down a single column: in the left hand pair, rows 1 to 6 are lengths and rows 7 to 28 are angles. A reader who takes the column heading at face value will read every angle as an Angstrom, which is wrong by two orders of magnitude. STANDARD UNCERTAINTY: the bracketed number in a value such as 1.331(4) or 111.3(2) is the standard uncertainty on the last digit or digits quoted, the usual crystallographic convention. It is NOT a footnote reference and NOT a count of anything. It is transcribed exactly as printed. TYPOGRAPHY: two values are printed with a space before the bracket, "116.81 (16)" and "120.1 (2)". The space is present in the text layer as well as on the image, so it is reproduced as printed; it is a typesetting artifact and carries no meaning. The page uses a decimal POINT throughout, not a German decimal comma.

This is the lower table on the page, with its caption printed here in full: "Tabelle 4: Bindungslängen [Å] und Bindungswinkel der Kristallmodifikation II". Note that this caption omits the [°] after "Bindungswinkel" that the Tabelle 3 caption on page 4 carries; that is how it is printed, not a transcription slip. The table continues onto page 6, which opens with "(fortgesetzt)" and the same four column headers. Only the 17 rows printed on THIS page are recorded here. It has no [00NN] marker of its own, so it is attached to the nearest preceding numbered paragraph, [0018] on page 3. COLUMN STRUCTURE, read off the image: four columns in two side by side pairs, Bindung | Å(°) | Bindung | Å(°). All 17 rows have all four cells filled. UNITS: as above, the label decides the unit, not the column. In this block the whole left hand pair is bond lengths in Angstrom, while the right hand pair switches partway down: rows 1 to 11 are lengths and rows 12 to 17 are angles in degrees, starting at F(2A)-C(10A)-F(1A) 106.2(6). STANDARD UNCERTAINTY: the bracketed number, for example the (16) in 1.7352(16) or the (11) in 1.361(11), is the standard uncertainty on the trailing digits. Not a footnote, not a count. The A and B suffixes on atom labels such as C(10A), F(2B) and O(3A) are the two alternative sites of a disordered group in the refined model; they are transcribed as printed and no attempt is made here to interpret the disorder.

blank_line_note: Blank lines inside paragraph zh/en were removed by the run owner. They came from the markdown-table convention this run uses to carry table content in the paragraph. build_enriched.py emits them into the enriched document, but english_by_line() in resolve_translations.py builds its `body` with `if t.strip()`, dropping blanks, while splitting the paragraph without dropping them. Any interior blank line therefore desynchronised the walk and it aborted, by design rather than guessing, which blocked verify.py for the whole run. Only whitespace-only lines were removed; every character of content is unchanged, asserted at the time of the edit.
